title: Games & Activities
text:
Time: 6:00–7:15 PM, including dinner · Materials: UNO, Jenga, printed Bingo cards, pens
As students arrive, leaders greet them by name and invite them into small mixed-age groups. In Human Bingo, find someone who matches a prompt such as “has helped a friend recently,” “knows a Bible verse by heart,” “plays an instrument,” or “is new to this group.” A student may sign only one or two squares per card, encouraging conversation beyond familiar friends.
Debrief: How does it feel when someone makes an effort to include you? (Romans 15:7)



Time: 7:30–8:30 PM · Materials: cups, string, tape, paper, blindfolds (optional), clue envelopes
Teams of four or five rotate through short cooperative stations:

Cup Stack Challenge: Stack cups using a shared rubber-band-and-string tool; no touching cups by hand.
Bridge Builders: Construct a paper bridge strong enough to support a small object.
Guided Journey: One student describes a simple obstacle path while a teammate follows with eyes open; teams practice listening and clear instructions.
Encouragement Relay: Each student shares a sincere affirmation or thanks for another teammate.

Scoring: Award points for collaboration, encouragement, and creativity—not only speed.
Debrief: What changed when everyone had a role? (1 Corinthians 12:12–27)



Time: 8:30–9:30 PM · Materials: printed Scripture passages, four puzzle envelopes, lockbox (optional)
Teams unlock four sequential clues using the Bible. Prepare one worksheet per station:

The Vine: John 15:1–5 — identify the vine, branches, and meaning of remaining in Christ.
The Body: 1 Corinthians 12:12–27 — match examples of spiritual gifts and mutual care.
The Fellowship: Hebrews 10:24–25 — solve a word-order puzzle about encouragement.
The New Command: John 13:34–35 — brainstorm a concrete way to demonstrate love.

Each solved station provides a word; together the four words form the closing statement: Abide. Belong. Encourage. Love. Leaders check completion; no student is locked in or isolated.
Debrief: What makes Christian community different from just being in a crowd?



Time: 9:30–10:15 PM · Materials: clearly marked approved play area
One player hides in an approved, supervised space. When another player finds that person, they quietly join them. The last player to find the group becomes the next hider. Use only adequately lit, accessible areas; no closets, bathrooms, stairwells, or locked rooms. Offer an accessible alternative team activity.
Debrief: How can we help someone who feels left out find belonging? (Ecclesiastes 4:9–10)



Time: 10:15–10:45 PM · Materials: sticky notes, markers, poster board
Invite students to anonymously or openly post three types of notes: “I’m thankful for…”, “Someone encouraged me when…”, and “This week I can encourage…”. Leaders screen notes before display to prevent hurtful content or accidental sharing of private information.
Debrief: What is one way words can build someone up? (1 Thessalonians 5:11)

title: Worship & Bible Study
text:
Worship: Abide Together
Choose two or three congregation-appropriate songs, rehearsed with the worship team. Possible contemporary selections include “Abide” (The Worship Initiative / Aaron Williams), “Build My Life” (Pat Barrett), and “The Blessing” (Kari Jobe, Cody Carnes, Elevation Worship). Confirm song arrangements, licensing, and any bilingual translations before use.

title: Worship & Bible Study
text:
Bible exposition (15–20 minutes)
Title: Connected to the True Vine
Primary passage: John 15:1–12

Point 1 — Connection to Jesus comes first (John 15:4–5)
A branch does not produce fruit by trying harder apart from the vine. We are invited to depend on Christ in prayer, Scripture, and daily trust—not merely to stay busy with church activities.


Point 2 — Abiding changes how we treat others (John 15:9–12)
Jesus links remaining in His love with obeying His command to love one another. Christian connection is expressed in concrete acts of patience, forgiveness, inclusion, and service.


Point 3 — We help one another stay connected (Hebrews 10:24–25)
Believers gather not simply to attend events, but to encourage one another toward love and good works. Students can become that support system for one another.

title: Worship & Bible Study
text:
Small-group discussion (15–20 minutes)

When do you feel most connected to God? What distracts you?
What makes it difficult to form real friendships—even at church?
What does Jesus mean by “abide in me” in everyday student life?
What can our youth group do to welcome someone who is new or quiet?
What one practical step will you take this week to encourage another person?

Leader guidance: Students may pass on personal questions. Do not pressure anyone to share private struggles publicly. Follow church safeguarding policies when a student discloses a safety concern.

title: Worship & Bible Study
text:
Prayer partners (12:00–12:30 AM)
Pair or group students with clear leader visibility. Invite them to share one low-pressure prayer request, then pray briefly for one another. Provide a silent reflection option for students who prefer not to speak. Close by praying for the entire youth community.
